title: Dr. Kevin Rudd Discusses China on the Ezra Klein Show
text:
Dr. Kevin Rudd Discusses China on the Ezra Klein Show

The New York Times

The Ezra Klein Show/The New York Times

The Honorable Dr. Kevin Rudd AC, Global President and CEO of the Asia Society, joined The New York Times podcast "The Ezra Klein Show" in July 2026 for a wide-ranging conversation on Chinese President Xi Jinping's ideological worldview and its consequences for China's economy, the U.S.-China relationship, and the future of cross-Strait relations. Dr. Rudd traced Xi's rise from vice mayor of Xiamen — where the two would-be leaders first met in the 1980s  — to China's paramount leader. Drawing on Dr. Rudd's book On Xi Jinping: How Xi's Marxist Nationalism Is Shaping China and the World, Dr. Rudd explained how Xi has moved China toward what Rudd characterizes as Marxist-Leninist nationalism: a shift to the Marxist left in the economy, a tightening of Leninist party control over politics and society, and a shift to the nationalist right in foreign policy. Dr. Rudd cautioned American policymakers against complacency about China's economic trajectory, noting that slowing growth and demographic headwinds have not altered Xi's core objective of building the world's most powerful industrial state. "Never underestimate Xi Jinping. Never, ever, underestimate him," Dr. Rudd told Klein. On the U.S.-China relationship, Dr. Rudd assessed the new "constructive strategic stability" framework announced at the recent Beijing summit between President Trump and President Xi. Dr. Rudd also restated the case for his long-standing framework of managed strategic competition: maintaining deterrence around strategic red lines, allowing full and open competition across the economic and technological domains, and cooperating in areas of mutual interest such as artificial intelligence governance and global public health. Dr. Rudd identified 2028 as a period of elevated risk in the Taiwan Strait due to the confluence of Taiwan's presidential election in January 2028, XI's expected reappointment as general secretary, and the U.S. presidential election. "My concern as an analyst is: Could [Xi] arrive at a conclusion through a bout of excessive self-confidence that a unique opportunity has arisen? The danger is that he actually miscalculates," Dr. Rudd said. Asked what a wise American policy would look like, Dr. Rudd argued for sustained deterrence as the most effective approach: one that preserves the status quo across the Taiwan Strait and kicks "the ball down the road for future generations who will be much wiser than us to solve this intractable problem." Watch the full conversation on YouTube or read an edited transcript on The New York Times website.
